findings.name: accounts-api
findings.root_cause: Init container wait-for-db loops forever because it probes host 'accounts-db:5432', but no Service named accounts-db exists in the namespace — the database is exposed as Service 'accounts-database' (ready endpoint on 5432) — so the pod never leaves Init:Running and the main container never starts.
findings.fix: Change the init container command to probe 'accounts-database:5432' instead of 'accounts-db:5432' (or add a Service alias named accounts-db).

diagnosis.summary: accounts-api has been stuck in Init:Running for ~20 minutes. Its init container wait-for-db runs `until nc -z -w 2 accounts-db 5432`, but the only Service in the accounts namespace is 'accounts-database' (port 5432, with one ready endpoint), so the hostname 'accounts-db' never resolves/accepts and the init loop spins indefinitely, blocking the accounts-api container from starting. Fix: point the init container at accounts-database:5432."

findings.name: stock-db
findings.root_cause: stock-db container is OOMKilled (exit 137) because its memory limit of 24Mi is far below what the workload needs once it starts "loading stock index into memory"; the DB restarts in BackOff and never serves 5432, so stock-api's connection attempts fail and it exits 1.
findings.fix: Raise the stock-db memory request/limit (e.g. to 128Mi or more based on observed usage) so the container survives loading the stock index into memory.

diagnosis.summary: stock-api crash-loops because its dependency stock-db is down: the stock-db container hits its 24Mi memory limit while loading the stock index into memory and is OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts, BackOff), so port 5432 is unreachable and stock-api exits with \"ERROR: stock-db:5432 unreachable\" (exit 1). Root cause is the undersized memory limit on Deployment stock-db; stock-api is a victim and should recover once stock-db stays up.

diagnosis.summary: smtp-relay is NOT down: its pod is scheduled and the Service has 1 ready endpoint on port 25. findings.name: nightly-export
findings.root_cause: Both pods of nightly-export exit 2 with "permission denied: cannot write /exports/orders-2026-09-27.csv"; the pod mounts no writable volume for /exports (only the serviceaccount token), so the export file is never written and the Job hit BackoffLimitExceeded.
findings.fix: Give the job a writable destination: mount an emptyDir or PVC at /exports (and ensure the container user can write it), then re-run the job.

diagnosis.summary: The nightly-export Job in exports failed both attempts (exit code 2, BackoffLimitExceeded). The container log shows the failure: \"ERROR: permission denied: cannot write /exports/orders-2026-09-27.csv\". The pod spec has no volumes mounted for /exports (only the default serviceaccount token), so there is no writable backing store for the export path — hence no file was produced last night. Fix: add a writable volume (emptyDir/PVC) at /exports on the Job's pod template and re-run."

findings.name: thumbnailer
findings.root_cause: The log-shipper sidecar cannot reach the upstream collector, so it buffers 4Mi batches into the shared emptyDir /buffer; its 20Mi ephemeral-storage limit is exceeded within minutes and kubelet evicts the whole pod (exit 137), which the Deployment immediately replaces — repeating every few minutes.
findings.fix: Raise/remove the log-shipper ephemeral-storage limit or cap/rotate buffered files in /buffer; separately restore connectivity to the upstream collector so buffering stops.

diagnosis.summary: thumbnailer pods are repeatedly evicted: the log-shipper sidecar's upstream collector is unreachable, so it writes 4Mi batches into the emptyDir /buffer until the pod's 20Mi ephemeral-storage limit is hit; kubelet evicts the pod (~every minute) and the Deployment recreates it. Two Failed/Evicted pods and matching Evicted events confirm the loop. Fix belongs in the thumbnailer Deployment spec (storage limit/buffering behavior) plus restoring collector connectivity."

diagnosis.summary: reports/report-worker crash-loops with OOMKilled (exit 137), restarts=3, ready 0/1. Root cause is the Deployment spec (command + tight memory limit). Fix: remove the /dev/zero tail or redirect its output, and size the memory limit appropriately."
